text:
maya: noticing repeated p95 latency jumps for medium models in eu-west-1 since the 03:00 deploy. spikes look correlated with scale-outs, not steady load. examples: p95 ~420ms -> 1.2s for 30s windows.

zane: saw that on the dashboard, thanks for flagging. autoscaler logs show scale events every ~90s for the same pool. suspicious oscillation.

ryan: checking profiler traces now. initial read: a bunch of kernel_fallback events and long kernel_compile times around the same timestamps. attaching short dump: 

```
# profiler extract
timestamp 1770023218 model-id redwood-gpt-medium
kernel_select: amx_q8 -> amx_f16_fallback
jit_compile_ms: 340, 298, 410
kv_cache_miss_rate: 0.26
batch_size_seen: 1..8 (bursty)
```

anika: interesting — batch sizes are all over the place which defeats continuous batching heuristics. when the autoscaler adds nodes we briefly push tiny concurrent tails that don't join batches. then kernels JIT or fallback which blocks other in-flight requests.

maya: also seeing KV cache cold-starts after scale-up. kv cache warmup is async, so first few requests pay extra. miss rate spikes coincide with node provisioning.

ops-bot: deploy 03:02 completed. autoscaler: increased pool from 6->10 at 03:09; decreased 10->6 at 03:12.

zane: that scale down at 03:12 is too fast — warm pool churn. we likely need a longer stabilization window to avoid churn.

ryan: another detail: GPU allocation logs show noisy-neighbor throttles on some hosts: vGPU utilization bursts at provisioning time, driver-level page faults increase, causing >200ms init delays for some kernels.

infra-sre-bot: recorded host failures: host-42 had 3 transient PCI resets between 03:08-03:11.

anika: putting it together: autoscaler triggers frequent adds/removes; new nodes cause kernel JIT & KV cold misses; some hosts have noisy neighbor effects prolonging GPU readiness — combined produces p95 spikes.

devex: any quick mitigations we can flip now?

maya: short-term suggestions: 1) bump warm pool min capacity for this pool from 6 -> 8 to reduce scale-outs, 2) increase scale-down delay from 3m -> 8m, 3) force precompile of problematic kernels during provisioning (rictl run-init-script) and pre-warm KV cache for pinned models.

zane: I can roll the warm-pool change and scale-down window now. will also add a temporary routing policy to avoid host-42.

ryan: I'll prepare a one-off init script to run on newly provisioned nodes that runs the heavy kernels once and loads keys into KV cache. snippet: 

```
rictl ssh run --hosts $NEW_HOSTS -- "python -m infra.prewarm --models redwood-gpt-medium --warm-keys 1000"
```

maya: we'll need a follow-up to fix batching heuristics: current batching timeout is 8ms for small sequences; that is too low for these jittery scale events. increase to 20ms and add an adaptive backoff when node join rate > X/min. that should let more requests coalesce.

anika: also propose we add a metric and alert: kernel_fallback_rate and kv_miss_rate per-pool with a paging threshold. helps catch regressions fast.

infra-sre-bot: created incident ticket INC-2026-autoscale-jitter (link: https://redwood/incident/INC-2026).

zane: rolling warm-pool change now, ETA 2m. tagging @ops-bot for host-42 drain.

ops-bot: host-42 draining initiated.

maya: thanks — once warm pool bump lands we'll monitor p95 across next 30m and decide on the prewarm rollout.

devex: can we add a short playbook entry for this pattern? autoscale oscillation -> kernel JIT + KV cold -> noisy-host amplifies. I can draft.

ryan: assigning follow-ups: ryan: prewarm init script + runbook; zane: warm-pool + scale-down tweak + host drain; anika: metric/alert + batching heuristic proposal.

maya: ack. will keep monitoring. ping if p95 > 800ms again. :eyes:
